issue.title: handle_accepted_plan's second epic SDD-commit-failure branch is unreachable for epics
issue.description:
Discovered while landing epic sase-fl (not caused by it — the not-is_epic gating predates sase-fl, introduced by commit 33d30ba0f "feat: make epic approval launches host-owned (sase-64.3)" on 2026-07-15).

In src/sase/axe/run_agent_exec_plan_accept.py::handle_accepted_plan, the SDD-commit try/except block (~lines 515-548) that can set store_unusable_error and required_sdd_commit_succeeded=False is entirely gated on `not is_epic`:

    if should_commit and sdd_plan_name and not is_epic:
        ...
    elif should_commit and not is_epic:
        required_sdd_commit_succeeded = False

For is_epic == True, neither branch executes, so no exception can be raised inside that try body for an epic, so store_unusable_error can never be set there and required_sdd_commit_succeeded stays True (its initialized default) for every epic. Two consequences:

1. The second `if is_epic and store_unusable_error is not None:` check at line 550 (which calls _record_epic_store_failure) can never fire for an epic — it is dead code specific to the epic path.
2. The `if not required_sdd_commit_succeeded:` warning block at handle_accepted_plan's epic return (~line 571: "Approved epic prompt archive entry could not be committed; the host-owned epic launch continues independently") is also unreachable dead code for the same reason.

Confirmed still present at sase-fl's HEAD (b5c78f972): epic sase-fl's phase sase-fl.1 refactored the store-failure recording into _record_epic_store_failure() and _epic_launch_is_host_owned(), and explicitly verified/documented that the fallthrough after the FIRST failure branch is safe (not-is_epic-gated code below it never dereferences sdd_store/sdd_plan_path) — but did not change the not-is_epic gating on the SECOND try body itself, so the dead-code condition this task describes is unchanged.

Fix: either wire the epic prompt-archive commit path through this second try/except so a real epic SDD-commit failure can actually be recorded and surfaced (matching the intent of the "prompt archive entry could not be committed" warning), or remove the unreachable is_epic branch/warning if epic prompt-archive commits are deliberately never expected to fail here for a different reason. Read the surrounding SDD-commit flow in src/sase/axe/run_agent_exec_plan_accept.py before choosing; verify the choice against how sdd_commit_paths / commit_sdd_store_files are used for epics elsewhere in the same function.

payload.entry: Backlog triage 2026-08-06 (master 25285417d), closed as one group. Each was verified as described but none is currently costing anyone anything: sase-fm — 'note' really is missing from _MUTATING_VERBS in src/sase/main/bead_fast_path.py (confirmed at HEAD: the frozenset is {'+1','close','create','open','ref','rm','update'}), but it is a sandbox-guard bypass with no observed bad write, so it protects tests from themselves rather than protecting production state. sase-fn — unreachable epic-path code in run_agent_exec_plan_accept.py; a cleanup with zero behavioral consequence either way. sase-gb — confirmed at HEAD that src/sase/sdd/_write.py still projects (line 85) before validating (line 95), but the bead itself records that sase-g4's approval gate rejects a malformed plan before this path runs, making it defence in depth against a future non-approval caller. sase-gd — the dry-run 'Archived' line does overclaim, but sase-g4 already removed the specific defect that line once hid. sase-ga — a leading unknown plan-header key going undiagnosed is, in the bead's own words, 'small but real', and the fix lives cross-repo in sase-core with a false-positive risk on ordinary prose bullets. Reopen any of these with a +1 if one actually bites — sase-fm in particular is worth a +1 the moment an unsandboxed 'sase bead note' is seen writing outside a test's store.

payload.close_reason: Backlog triage 2026-08-06: defence-in-depth, dead code, or misleading-but-harmless output with no currently-reproducing user-visible failure. Cut to bring the ready task queue from 30 to 7.
